title: Pods fail to start with FailedCreate event and 'exceeded quota' message in OpenShift
issue:
Pods cannot be created in an OpenShift namespace. The ReplicaSet or Deployment shows FailedCreate events in 'oc describe'. The event message contains text similar to:

  Error creating: pods "myapp-7d9f8b6c5-" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-resources, requested: requests.cpu=500m, used: requests.cpu=3500m, limited: requests.cpu=4

The pods remain in Pending state and new replicas cannot be scheduled.
resolution:
1. Identify the resource quota in the affected namespace:
   oc get resourcequota -n <namespace>
   oc describe resourcequota compute-resources -n <namespace>

2. Compare used vs. hard limits. If usage is at or near the limit, either:
   a. Reduce resource requests on the affected Deployment:
      oc set resources deployment/<name> --requests=cpu=200m,memory=256Mi -n <namespace>

   b. Or increase the ResourceQuota limit (requires cluster-admin):
      oc edit resourcequota compute-resources -n <namespace>
      # Increase the hard.requests.cpu or hard.memory value

3. If other Pods are consuming quota unexpectedly, identify them:
   oc get pods -n <namespace> -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,CPU_REQ:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.cpu,MEM_REQ:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.memory'

4. After adjusting, verify the Deployment recovers:
   oc rollout status deployment/<name> -n <namespace>
root_cause: The namespace ResourceQuota limit for CPU or memory requests has been reached. OpenShift enforces ResourceQuota at admission time; any new Pod whose resource requests would cause the namespace total to exceed the quota hard limit is rejected with a 'forbidden: exceeded quota' error. This results in FailedCreate events on the owning ReplicaSet or StatefulSet.

title: How to check and manage ResourceQuota usage in OpenShift namespaces
issue: Administrators or developers need to understand the current ResourceQuota consumption in an OpenShift namespace to determine why pods are not starting, or to plan capacity. It is not immediately obvious which quota dimension (CPU, memory, PVC count, object count) is exhausted.
resolution:
Check all quotas and their current usage:
  oc get resourcequota -n <namespace>
  oc describe resourcequota -n <namespace>

The 'Used' column shows current consumption and 'Hard' shows the limit. A namespace may have multiple ResourceQuota objects (e.g. compute-resources, object-counts).

To check quota across all namespaces (cluster-admin):
  oc get resourcequota --all-namespaces

To see per-pod resource requests contributing to quota:
  oc get pods -n <namespace> -o json | jq '.items[].spec.containers[].resources.requests'

To temporarily increase a quota for testing (cluster-admin):
  oc patch resourcequota compute-resources -n <namespace> -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"requests.cpu":"8"}}}'

To set a LimitRange so pods without explicit requests inherit defaults (preventing unbounded quota consumption):
  oc create -f limitrange.yaml -n <namespace>
root_cause: ResourceQuota objects are defined per namespace by cluster administrators to prevent any single namespace from consuming all cluster resources. When a namespace's cumulative resource requests (across all Pods) reach the hard limit, no new Pods can be admitted until existing Pods are deleted or the quota is increased.

title: ReplicaSet stuck with FailedCreate - pods forbidden due to exceeded memory quota in OpenShift
issue:
A Deployment or ReplicaSet is unable to create pods. 'oc describe rs <replicaset-name>' shows repeated FailedCreate Warning events:

  Warning  FailedCreate  replicaset-controller  Error creating: pods "<name>" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-resources, requested: limits.memory=512Mi, used: limits.memory=7680Mi, limited: limits.memory=8Gi

Existing pods in the namespace are running but no new pods can be scheduled.
resolution:
1. Confirm the quota breach:
   oc describe resourcequota -n <namespace>

2. Options to resolve:

   Option A - Reduce memory limits on the Deployment:
     oc set resources deployment/<name> -n <namespace> \
       --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=128Mi

   Option B - Delete unused or completed pods to free quota:
     oc delete pod --field-selector=status.phase==Succeeded -n <namespace>
     oc delete pod --field-selector=status.phase==Failed -n <namespace>

   Option C - Request a quota increase from the cluster administrator:
     The admin can edit the ResourceQuota object:
     oc edit resourcequota compute-resources -n <namespace>

3. Force the ReplicaSet to retry after quota is freed:
   oc rollout restart deployment/<name> -n <namespace>

4. Verify pods come up:
   oc get pods -n <namespace> -w
root_cause: The namespace memory limit quota (limits.memory) is fully consumed by running pods. OpenShift's admission controller rejects any new pod that would cause the total namespace memory limits to exceed the ResourceQuota hard limit. Completed or failed pods that have not been garbage-collected still count toward quota until they are deleted.
